questions.question: Pramod sold 154 chairs and had a gain equal to the selling price of 54 chairs. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Selling Price (SP) of 1 chair be 1 unit.

Total SP of 154 chairs = 154 units.

Profit = SP of 54 chairs = 54 units.

Cost Price (CP) = Total SP − Profit = 154 − 54 = 100 units.

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (54 ÷ 100) × 100 = 54%.

**∴ The correct answer is 54%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total chairs sold = 154

Profit = Selling Price (SP) of 54

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought an article for ₹520. At what price (in ₹) should he sell the article to make 20% profit?

If Cost Price is 5 parts, Profit is 1 part, so Selling Price = 6 parts.

**Calculations:**

Loss Formula

Marked Price & Discount

questions.question: The greatest number, which divides 943 and 1957 to leave 7 and 1 respectively as remainders, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Required number = HCF of (First Number − Remainder 1) and (Second Number − Remainder 2)

Required number = HCF(943 − 7, 1957 − 1)

Required number = HCF(936, 1956)

Since 936 = 12 × 78 and 1956 = 12 × 163, and 163 is a prime number, their highest common factor is 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number = 943, Remainder = 7

Second number = 1957, Remainder = 1

**Formula Used:**

Greatest number dividing x and y leaving remainders a and b = HCF of (x − a) and (y − b)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number 1 = 943 − 7 = 936

⇒ Number 2 = 1957 − 1 = 1956

⇒ Prime factorization of 936 = 2³ × 3² × 13

⇒ Prime factorization of 1956 = 2² × 3 × 163

⇒ Common prime factors = 2² and 3

⇒ HCF = 2² × 3 = 4 × 3 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF for given Remainders

The greatest number that divides x, y, and z leaving remainders a, b, and c respectively is given by HCF of (x − a), (y − b), and (z − c).

HCF for Same Remainder

The greatest number that divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder in each case is given by HCF of |x − y|, |y − z|, and |z − x|.

LCM for Same Remainder

The least number which when divided by x, y, and z leaves the same remainder r in each case is given by LCM(x, y, z) + r.

Relationship between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers a and b: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.
</p

questions.question: The price (per litre) of petrol increases by 40%. By what percent should its consumption be reduced such that the expenditure on it increases by 19% only?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial expenditure on petrol be 100.

Due to a 40% increase in price, the expected expenditure becomes 140.

However, the actual new expenditure is only allowed to increase by 19%, making it 119.

Required reduction in consumption (calculated on the new base of 140) = 140 − 119 = 21.

Percentage reduction = (21 ÷ 140) × 100 = 15%.

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price increase = 40%

Expenditure increase = 19%

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 
 Base = 100

 
 New Price = 140

 
 New Exp = 119

 
 
• 
 Price +40%

 
 
• 
 Exp +19%

 
 
• 
 Reduce by 21

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial price be 100 and the initial consumption be 100 units.

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 100 × 100 = 10000

⇒ New Price after 40% increase = 100 + 40 = 140

⇒ New Expenditure after 19% increase = 10000 × 1.19 = 11900

⇒ New Consumption = New Expenditure ÷ New Price

⇒ New Consumption = 11900 ÷ 140 = 85 units

⇒ Decrease in Consumption = Initial Consumption − New Consumption

⇒ Decrease in Consumption = 100 − 85 = 15 units

⇒ Percentage decrease = (15 ÷ 100) × 100 = 15%

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

1. Price-Consumption-Expenditure Rule

Total Expenditure = Price × Consumption. If expenditure is kept constant, an increase in price results in a proportionally inverse decrease in consumption.

2. Base Change Concept

Whenever a value is manipulated relative to a new changed value, the percentage change must always be calculated by dividing the absolute difference by the new base.

3. Percentage Decrease Formula

Percentage Decrease = (Decrease in Value ÷ Original Value) × 100.
</p

questions.question: The average age of 40 students of a class is 12 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 13 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Increase in average age = 13 − 12 = 1 year.

Number of students originally = 40.

Teacher's age = New Average + (Initial Number of Students × Increase in Average)

Teacher's age = 13 + (40 × 1) = 53 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 53.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average age of 40 students = 12 years.

Average age of 41 people (40 students + 1 teacher) = 13 years.

**Formula Used:**

Total Age = Average Age × Number of People

 
 40 Students (Avg: 12)
 
 Teacher
 
• 
 Combined Average: 13 years
 

 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total age of 40 students = 40 × 12 = 480 years.

⇒ Total age of 41 people = 41 × 13 = 533 years.

⇒ Age of the teacher = (Total age of 41 people) − (Total age of 40 students)

⇒ Age of the teacher = 533 − 480

⇒ Age of the teacher = 53 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 53.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

New Member Age Formula

When a person joins a group, their age = New Average + (Old Number of Members × Change in Average).

Leaving Member Age Formula

When a person leaves a group, their age = Old Average + (New Number of Members × Change in Average).

Weighted Average

Combined Average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is count and x is the individual average.</p

questions.question: If the income of Ravi is 24% more than that of Ram, then by what percentage is the income of Ram less than that of Ravi?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If A is r% more than B, then B is less than A by [r / (100 + r)] × 100%.

Here, Ravi's income is 24% more than Ram's, so r = 24.

Required percentage = [24 / (100 + 24)] × 100%

⇒ Required percentage = (24 / 124) × 100% = (6 / 31) × 100% = 600/31%

**∴ The correct answer is 600/31%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ravi's income is 24% more than Ram's income.

**Formula Used:**

Percentage less = (Difference / Base Value) × 100

 Ram's Income (100)
 
 
 Ravi's Income (124)
 
 
 
 
• 
 +24
 
 Comparison Base = Ravi's Income (124)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Ram's income be 100 units.

⇒ Ravi's income = 100 + 24 = 124 units.

⇒ Difference between their incomes = 124 − 100 = 24 units.

⇒ We need to find the percentage by which Ram's income is less than Ravi's income.

⇒ Required percentage = (Difference / Ravi's income) × 100

⇒ Required percentage = (24 / 124) × 100

⇒ Required percentage = (6 / 31) × 100 = 600/31%

**∴ The correct answer is 600/31%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Base Change in Percentage

If A is x% less than B, then B is [x / (100 − x)] × 100% more than A. Reversing the base changes the percentage magnitude.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value is successively increased or decreased by a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by the formula (a + b + ab/100)%.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion Method

Converting percentage rates to fractions directly accelerates calculations. For example, 24% = 24/100 = 6/25. If value A is 6/25 more than B, then value B is 6/(25 + 6) = 6/31 less than A. Consequently, 6/31 × 100 = 600/31%.
</p

questions.question: The diagonals of a rhombus are 4 m and 6 m, respectively. Find its area (in m² ).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The area of a rhombus can be determined directly by halving the product of its diagonals.

Area = (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 2

Area = (4 × 6) ÷ 2 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12 m².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first diagonal (d₁) = 4 m

Length of second diagonal (d₂) = 6 m

**Formula Used:**

Area of a rhombus = ½ × d₁ × d₂

 

 
• 
 
• 
 

 d1 = 4 m
 d2 = 6 m
 Area of Rhombus

**Calculation:**

⇒ Area = ½ × 4 × 6

⇒ Area = 2 × 6

⇒ Area = 12 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 12 m².**

**__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Rhombus

The perimeter of a rhombus is calculated as 4 × side length, or P = 2 × √(d₁² + d₂²).

Side of a Rhombus

Since the diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at exactly 90°, the side length can be found using the Pythagoras theorem: side = ½ × √(d₁² + d₂²).

Area using Base and Height

Because a rhombus is a specific type of parallelogram, its area can also be computed directly using Area = base × perpendicular height.

questions.question: A and B can do a work in 30 days and 10 days respectively. If they start the work with A and work on alternate days, in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(30, 10) = 30 units.

Efficiency of A = 1 unit/day, B = 3 units/day.

Work in 1 cycle (2 days) = 1 + 3 = 4 units.

In 7 cycles (14 days), work = 7 × 4 = 28 units. Remaining = 30 − 28 = 2 units.

On 15th day, A does 1 unit. Remaining 1 unit is done by B in 1/3 day.

**∴ The correct answer is 15¹/₃ days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A alone = 30 days

Time taken by B alone = 10 days

They work on alternate days starting with A.

**Concept Used:**

Total Work = LCM of days taken by individuals

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 30
 30
 1
 
 

 B
 10
 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done in a 2-day cycle (Day 1: A, Day 2: B) = 1 + 3 = 4 units.

⇒ Work done in 7 complete cycles (14 days) = 7 × 4 = 28 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 30 − 28 = 2 units.

⇒ On the 15th day, it is A's turn. A completes 1 unit.

⇒ Remaining work = 2 − 1 = 1 unit.

⇒ On the 16th day, it is B's turn. Time taken by B to finish 1 unit = 1 ÷ 3 = 1/3 day.

⇒ Total time taken = 14 + 1 + 1/3 = 15¹/₃ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 15¹/₃ days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Working

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the work done in a complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and divide the total work by this cycle's work to find the number of full cycles and remaining work.

Work and Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. For a constant amount of work, if an individual takes more days, they have a proportionately lower efficiency.

Total Work Assumption

Assuming total work as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of individual completion times avoids fractions and strictly speeds up daily unit efficiency calculations.
</p

questions.question: A salesman offers a discount scheme of 'Buy 25 and get 5 free' on the purchase of notebooks in his shop. He professes that a notebook costs him ₹10, but in reality, it costs him ₹5. Find the difference between his profit percentage and scheme discount.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total CP for 30 notebooks (25 paid + 5 free) = 30 × ₹5 = ₹150

Total SP for 25 notebooks charged = 25 × ₹10 = ₹250

Profit % = [(250 − 150) ÷ 150] × 100 = 200/3 %

Discount % = [Free items ÷ Total items] × 100 = (5 ÷ 30) × 100 = 50/3 %

Difference = 200/3 % − 50/3 % = 150/3 % = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Scheme = Buy 25 get 5 free

Professed cost per notebook (Selling Price) = ₹10

Real cost per notebook (Cost Price) = ₹5

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = (Free Quantity ÷ Total Quantity) × 100

Profit % = (Total Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

 
 25 Paid Items

•

• 
 Total SP = 25 × ₹10 = ₹250
 
 
• 
 
•

 Total CP = 30 × ₹5 = ₹150

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total items given to the customer = 25 + 5 = 30 items

⇒ Discount % = (5 ÷ 30) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 6) × 100 = 50/3 %

⇒ Total CP of 30 notebooks = 30 × ₹5 = ₹150

⇒ Total SP of 25 notebooks = 25 × ₹10 = ₹250

⇒ Total Profit = Total SP − Total CP = 250 − 150 = ₹100

⇒ Profit % = (100 ÷ 150) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (2 ÷ 3) × 100 = 200/3 %

⇒ Difference = Profit % − Discount %

⇒ Difference = 200/3 % − 50/3 % = 150/3 % = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Discount % in Buy X Get Y Free

 18 : 42 :: 42 : 98

**Formula Used:**

Mean proportional of two numbers a and b = √(a × b)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mean proportional = √(18 × 98)

⇒ Mean proportional = √(9 × 2 × 2 × 49)

⇒ Mean proportional = 3 × 2 × 7 = 42

⇒ According to the given condition, 2A + 6 = 42

⇒ 2A = 42 − 6

⇒ 2A = 36

⇒ A = 18

**∴ The correct answer is A = 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Third Proportional

The third proportional of two numbers a and b is c, such that a : b :: b : c. Formula: c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

The fourth proportional of three numbers a, b, and c is d, such that a : b :: c : d. Formula: d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Compounded Ratio

When two or more ratios are multiplied together, it is called a compounded ratio. For given ratios a:b and c:d, the compounded ratio is ac:bd.
</p

questions.question: The average age of 35 students in a group is 15 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average age of the group increases by 1.25 years. What is the teacher's age (in years)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Teacher's Age = Old Average + (New Total Members × Increase in Average)

Teacher's Age = 15 + (36 × 1.25)

Teacher's Age = 15 + 45 = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Students = 35, Average age = 15 years

New average increase when teacher joins = 1.25 years

**Formula Used:**

Total Age = Average Age × Number of Persons

 Net Deviation Method
 
 
 Old Avg = 15

 
 Extra = 36 × 1.25 = 45

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Teacher's Age = 15 + 45 = 60

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total age of 35 students = 35 × 15 = 525 years

⇒ Total members including teacher = 35 + 1 = 36

⇒ New average age = 15 + 1.25 = 16.25 years

⇒ Total age of 36 members = 36 × 16.25 = 585 years

⇒ Teacher's age = Total age of 36 members − Total age of 35 students

⇒ Teacher's age = 585 − 525 = 60 years

**∴ The correct answer is 60 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Deviation Method for Averages

When a new entity joins a group and the average increases: New Value = Old Average + (Total Members × Increase in Average). This works seamlessly to avoid large multiplications.

Combined Average

The combined average of two distinct groups can be found using the formula: (N₁A₁ + N₂A₂) ÷ (N₁ + N₂), where N represents the number of items and A denotes the average of the respective groups.

Replacement Concept in Averages

If an existing member is replaced by a new person: New Person's Value = Replaced Person's Value + (Total Members × Change in Average).
</p

questions.question: Two trains having lengths of 340 m and 360 m are running at speeds of 80 km/h and 90 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed of trains in the same direction = 90 − 80 = 10 km/h.

Convert to m/s: 10 × (5/18) = 25/9 m/s.

Total distance to cross = Length of both trains = 340 + 360 = 700 m.

Time taken = Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 700 × (9/25) = 252 seconds.

Convert time to minutes = 252 ÷ 60 = 4.2 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.2 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the faster train (L₁) = 360 m

Length of the slower train (L₂) = 340 m

Speed of the faster train (S₁) = 90 km/h

Speed of the slower train (S₂) = 80 km/h

 
 360 m
 90 km/h →

 80 km/h →
 
 
• 
 Total Distance = 700 m

 Relative Speed = 90 − 80 = 10 km/h
 Time = 4.2 mins

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Same Direction) = S₁ − S₂

Time Taken = Total Length ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Length to cross = L₁ + L₂ = 360 + 340 = 700 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 90 − 80 = 10 km/h

⇒ Convert relative speed to m/s = 10 × (5/18) = 25/9 m/s

⇒ Time Taken (in seconds) = 700 ÷ (25/9)

⇒ Time Taken = (700 × 9) ÷ 25

⇒ Time Taken = 28 × 9 = 252 seconds

⇒ Convert seconds to minutes = 252 ÷ 60 = 4.2 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 4.2 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects travel in the same direction, their relative speed is calculated by taking the difference of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects travel towards each other in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Distance Covered in Train Crossings

When a train completely crosses another moving or stationary train, a platform, or a bridge, the total distance covered is always the sum of both their lengths (L₁ + L₂).

Speed Conversions

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s back to km/h, multiply by 18/5.
</p

questions.question: The distance from Chandigarh to Amritsar is covered in 4.5 hours at a speed of 50 km/hr. By how much should the speed (in km/hr) be increased to save 30 minutes of travel time?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time: S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂

⇒ 50 × 4.5 = S₂ × (4.5 − 0.5)

⇒ 225 = S₂ × 4

⇒ S₂ = 56.25 km/hr

Increase in speed = 56.25 − 50 = 6.25 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6.25 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial time (T₁) = 4.5 hours

Initial speed (S₁) = 50 km/hr

Time to be saved = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours

New time (T₂) = 4.5 − 0.5 = 4 hours

 
• 
 
 
 Chandigarh
 Amritsar
 Total Distance = 50 × 4.5 = 225 km
 Case 1: S = 50 km/hr, T = 4.5 hrs
 Case 2: New Speed, T = 4.0 hrs
 New Speed = 225 ÷ 4 = 56.25 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 50 × 4.5 = 225 km

⇒ New Speed (S₂) = Total Distance ÷ New Time

⇒ S₂ = 225 ÷ 4 = 56.25 km/hr

⇒ Required increase in speed = S₂ − S₁

⇒ Increase in speed = 56.25 − 50 = 6.25 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6.25 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Relationship of Speed and Time

When the distance remains constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T). Therefore, S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂.

Average Speed

Average Speed is the ratio of total distance traveled to the total time taken: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed is S₁ + S₂. When they move in the same direction, it is |S₁ − S₂|.
</p

questions.question: The greatest number, which divides 1477 and 671 to leave 0 and 6 respectively as remainders, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The greatest number dividing A and B with remainders R₁ and R₂ is the HCF of (A − R₁) and (B − R₂).

Required number = HCF of (1477 − 0) and (671 − 6)

Required number = HCF of 1477 and 665

Since 665 ends in 5, its factors are 5, 7, and 19. Checking the options, 7 divides both 1477 and 665 perfectly.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers to be divided = 1477 and 671

Remainders left = 0 and 6 respectively

**Formula Used:**

Required greatest number = HCF[(N₁ − R₁), (N₂ − R₂)]

**Calculations:**

⇒ First resulting number = 1477 − 0 = 1477

⇒ Second resulting number = 671 − 6 = 665

⇒ Prime factorization of 1477 = 7 × 211

⇒ Prime factorization of 665 = 5 × 133 = 5 × 7 × 19

⇒ The highest common factor (HCF) of 1477 and 665 is 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF for Equal Remainders

When the greatest number divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder in each case, the number is the HCF of |x − y|, |y − z|, and |z − x|.

LCM for Specific Remainders

The smallest number which when divided by a, b, and c leaves remainders p, q, and r respectively (where a−p = b−q = c−r = k) is given by (LCM of a, b, c) − k.

Relation between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is strictly equal to the product of their HCF and LCM (A × B = HCF × LCM).
</p
